items.explanation: 71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5) and no anticoagulant on any current or recent order; cardiology clinic notes from 2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28 list only tamsulosin. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft), which meets the guideline threshold (score >= 2 in a man) for recommended oral anticoagulation. No documented contraindication; the remote procedural-hemorrhage code is historical. Stroke-prevention therapy needs prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02; there is no prior citalopram order for this patient. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (5 days), so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 and first appears in that visit's medication list; the only earlier amiodarone was an inpatient course that ended 2025-01-26, more than nine months before. The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the earlier 30-day window is retained (due 2026-03-14) rather than the revised 14-day rule. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met (QTc ~484 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold).

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-04-10. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised 14-day window applies, so an ECG was due by 2026-04-24. The only ECG in the chart, 107859369, was recorded 2026-04-29 - 19 days after the start and 5 days after the deadline - so the monitoring requirement was not met within the required time and is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-01 and first appears in that visit's medication list; the only prior exposure was a 3-day inpatient course ending 2026-01-01. Start on/after 3/1/2026 means a 14-day window, due 2026-08-15. The patient's only ECG is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, before the start, and no ECG has been obtained since, so the requirement is overdue.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was restarted at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (previous exposure was inpatient, ended 2024-09-18), so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 2026-08-25 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - with the report requested but not yet received. That outside tracing could satisfy the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-09-15; the only prior exposure was inpatient injections in Feb-Mar 2025. The revised 14-day window applies, so an ECG is due by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the deadline falls after the 2026-09-24 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

Cardiology Clinic clinician note of 2026-09-01 documents a genuine dose change: 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR.' Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), inside the window, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation-clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 documents a dose change made under the clinic standing order: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin, so this triggers the 3/1/2026 requirement for an INR within 7 days, due 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change (the 3.4 was a patient-reported home value, not a chart result), and no INR has been resulted since, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman with documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300) and no anticoagulant on any current order; clinic notes through 2026-03-08 list only famotidine and metoprolol. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior cerebral infarction/stroke = 2, female), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). Documented thrombocytopenia is a bleeding-risk modifier, not a stated contraindication, and needs clinician review rather than silent omission of therapy.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg BID was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2026-12-28) and is current at the evaluation time, and the same-day clinic note says 'continue current regimen'. Active anticoagulation after a major GI bleed that was deliberately held requires prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note intended a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, and that note's medication list itself shows both agents. Overlapping DOAC therapy is a bleeding hazard and must be reconciled.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular ventricular response with no discernible P waves at a mean rate of ~136-142 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm is contradicted by the same-day tracings and the chart rhythm/rate needs correction.

Patient is on the QT watch-list drug amiodarone 200 mg daily, continuously refilled (current order 2026-08-22 to 2027-01-05). Her most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with a markedly broad T wave: QT ~556 ms, RR 1044 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~544 ms, well above the clinic's 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14) are not repleted-high; prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient takes the QT watch-list drug escitalopram 10 mg daily (current order 2026-04-23 to 2027-01-02). Most recent ECG (108018814, 2023-10-08) is sinus at 68 bpm with QT ~493 ms and RR 880 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~525 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. The 2024-05-14 note characterising this tracing as 'QT acceptable' understates it. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2025-08-23) are normal, so the prolongation is not explained by electrolytes; prescriber review required.

Patient takes the QT watch-list drug citalopram 40 mg daily (a dose above the 20 mg/day maximum advised in the elderly; current order 2026-05-29 to 2026-12-25). Most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) is sinus at 70 bpm with a very broad T wave: QT ~510 ms, RR 856 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~551 ms, above the 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal; prescriber review of citalopram dose and a repeat ECG are required.

Patient is on the QT watch-list drug amiodarone 200 mg daily (current order 2026-07-29 to 2027-01-05) together with warfarin. Most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) is sinus at 62 bpm with QT ~528 ms and RR 968 ms, QTc (Bazett) ~536 ms, above the clinic's 500 ms threshold. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (2026-04-20) are normal, so prescriber review of amiodarone is required.

items.explanation: 71-year-old man with documented atrial fibrillation (Condition 7010d0e5) and no anticoagulant on any current or recent order; cardiology clinic notes from 2025-10-10 through 2026-07-28 list only tamsulosin. CHA2DS2-VASc 3 (hypertension, age 65-74, vascular disease - coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery with prior bypass/graft), which meets the guideline threshold (score >= 2 in a man) for recommended oral anticoagulation. No documented contraindication; the remote procedural-hemorrhage code is historical. Stroke-prevention therapy needs prescriber review.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-03-02; there is no prior citalopram order for this patient. Because the start is on/after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies: ECG within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-03-16. ECG 104882441 was obtained at the 2026-03-07 clinic visit (5 days), so the requirement was met.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list) was started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2025-11-10 and first appears in that visit's medication list; the only earlier amiodarone was an inpatient course that ended 2025-01-26, more than nine months before. The start falls between 9/1/2025 and 2/28/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list) was first started at the cardiology clinic visit of 2026-02-12. The start precedes 3/1/2026, so the earlier 30-day window is retained (due 2026-03-14) rather than the revised 14-day rule. ECG 101538691 was obtained 2026-03-08, 24 days after the start, so the requirement was met (QTc ~484 ms, below the 500 ms review threshold).

Cardiology Clinic clinician note of 2026-09-01 documents a genuine dose change: 'INR today 1.6, subtherapeutic. Increase warfarin to 7.5 mg daily; recheck INR.' Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, by 2026-09-08. INR 2.3 was resulted 2026-09-05 (Observation d6b3bad5), inside the window, so the requirement was met.

Anticoagulation-clinic pharmacist note of 2026-09-10 documents a dose change made under the clinic standing order: home INR 3.4, warfarin decreased from 5 mg to 4 mg daily. Clinic pharmacists are authorised to adjust warfarin, so this triggers the 3/1/2026 requirement for an INR within 7 days, due 2026-09-17. The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change (the 3.4 was a patient-reported home value, not a chart result), and no INR has been resulted since, so the follow-up is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

71-year-old woman with documented paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (Condition 66dd1300) and no anticoagulant on any current order; clinic notes through 2026-03-08 list only famotidine and metoprolol. CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (hypertension, age 65-74, prior cerebral infarction/stroke = 2, female), so guideline-directed oral anticoagulation is recommended (Class 1). Documented thrombocytopenia is a bleeding-risk modifier, not a stated contraindication, and needs clinician review rather than silent omission of therapy.

Outside-records summary of 2026-08-12 documents an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (hemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly HELD at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban 5 mg BID was re-ordered on 2026-08-20 (valid to 2026-12-28) and is current at the evaluation time, and the same-day clinic note says 'continue current regimen'. Active anticoagulation after a major GI bleed that was deliberately held requires prescriber review.

Two different oral anticoagulants are simultaneously current: apixaban 5 mg BID (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-26) and rivaroxaban 20 mg daily (ordered 2026-07-15, valid to 2026-12-25). The 2026-07-15 cardiology note intended a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban but the rivaroxaban order was never stopped, and that note's medication list itself shows both agents. Overlapping DOAC therapy is a bleeding hazard and must be reconciled.
